poems.title: ENE Repeat
poems.text:
Some films entertain you.
Some make you laugh, cry, reminisce, and fall in love with cinema all over again.
And then there are films that hold up a mirror, let you recognise yourself in fictional people, and keep you thinking about life long after the credits roll.

ENE Repeat is one of those films for me.

I loved it, and not just for the friendship, the humour, the romance, or the filmmaking.
I loved it because it gathers the insecurities, imperfections, fears, dreams, and little victories that make us human, and places them gently in front of us.
I walked in to watch a film.
I walked out having looked at myself.

Growing up, it says, isn't about having everything figured out.
Sometimes it's about learning to live with what we haven't figured out yet.

## The Director: Tharun Bhascker, Who Trusts the Ordinary
Tharun Bhascker deserves immense appreciation for his writing, direction, and storytelling.

What I loved most was his restraint.
He never strains to make every moment extraordinary.
He lets ordinary conversations, awkward silences, little arguments, and random jokes carry the story.
That is where the magic lives.

Life rarely announces its most important moments.
They happen on a beach, over a meal, in a moment of hesitation, or while sitting beside someone without knowing what to say.
The film knows this, and it made me remember how many of my own most important moments arrived quietly, dressed as nothing.

It also shows friendship at its least polished: insecure, stubborn, immature, frightened, and sometimes unable to say what it feels.
That is exactly why it hurts in the right places.

And it reminds me what cinema is for.
Films aren't only an escape from reality.
Sometimes they are how we understand it.
They motivate us, challenge us, and occasionally give us the courage to face what we've been avoiding.

## The Music: Vivek Sagar, Where Silence Sings
I believe music is magic.
For me it was, is, and will always be everything.
Every emotion I feel, every memory I carry, every feeling I can't put into words finds its way into music.

And Vivek Sagar proves once again why he is a maestro.

What moved me was the subtlety.
The music never begs you to feel something.
It simply lives inside the scene, sometimes almost unnoticed, and says what words cannot.
There is a rare beauty in music that knows when to speak and when to stay silent.
Sometimes the smallest arrangement turns an ordinary moment into an unforgettable one.
Sometimes silence itself becomes part of the composition.

Music doesn't have to dominate a scene to define it.
Sometimes it only has to breathe beside it.

Kudos to Vivek Sagar and the entire music team.
What a gift to this film.

## Shirley: The Assurance of Simply Showing Up
Shirley is a beautiful character.
Her simplicity, her faith in Vivek, and her willingness to stand beside him make her special.

She believes in him even when he can't believe in himself.
She knows it may hurt her, and she still wants the best for him.
She doesn't demand that he become someone else.
She only wants to see him do better.
And even when distance grew between them, she was ready to leave everything behind and come for him.

Someone who doesn't have all the answers but still chooses to walk beside you is a rare kind of love.
Watching her, I wondered how many Shirleys I may have failed to notice because I was too busy fighting myself.

Sometimes assurance isn't a grand declaration.
Sometimes it is simply showing up.

## Keerthana: Strength in Vulnerability
Keerthana is a character I truly loved.
Her passion, innocence, vulnerability, and maturity make an unusual and lovely combination.

I loved her conversation with Ankit and the innocence with which she approaches things.
I loved how she tried to hold a situation together even when circumstances were against her.
Her moments of panic make her feel real.
She isn't written as someone with everything figured out.
She has her own boundaries, her own fears, her own journey.
I especially appreciated her need for privacy and space to understand things for herself.

And Karthik gives her that space.
He learns that being with someone doesn't mean controlling their time, thoughts, or decisions.
In letting her grow, he lets himself grow too.

Sometimes the best thing you can do for someone is give them room to discover themselves.

## The Boys: Four Fragments of One Human Being
Somewhere, I feel Tharun Bhascker understood that these four boys may not be four different people at all.
They may be four fragments of a single human being, four versions of ourselves that surface as we move through life.
I found every one of them somewhere inside me.

## Upendra (Uppu): The Glue
Perhaps the most underrated character in the entire film.

The way he stands with his friends, stands for his friends, and never lets go of the thought of keeping them together is something truly special.
He is the glue of this friendship.

I have tried to be that person myself: resolving things, keeping people close, trying to stop a friendship from falling apart.
It is much harder than it looks.
People notice the friendship, but rarely the one quietly working to preserve it.
Someone takes up that burden only because they can't bear to watch something they love fall apart.

But friendship should never be one person's responsibility.
Everyone has to hold on.

## Kaushik: The Rubber Band and the Small Victories
Abhinav's portrayal of Kaushik was wonderful.
Kaushik and Uppu feel like two rubber bands holding the whole friendship together, pulling in different directions yet never letting it snap.

What stays with me is that no amount of humiliation stops Kaushik from doing the work anyway.
He doesn't let a setback become the end of the road.
And he has one more gift: he enjoys small successes.
We spend so much of life waiting for something extraordinary that we forget the little things happening right in front of us, like a finished task, a good conversation, or a moment of happiness.

Not everything needs to be a milestone.
Sometimes the smallest victories deserve the biggest smiles.

I don't always practise this, but every now and then I try.
It is something I would love to learn from him.

## Karthik: The Fear of Losing
What a performance.

The beach conversation with Keerthana is one of my favourite scenes in the entire film.
His admission of fear, and his regret over people who left his life, made it deeply moving.

Even the smallest gap or insecurity can make us believe we are being abandoned.
Sometimes we leave people before they can leave us.
Sometimes we create the distance ourselves, out of fear of being hurt, and then carry the regret for years, long after that person has forgotten we ever existed.

What makes Karthik so interesting is that his fear doesn't vanish just because someone wants to enter his life.
He is afraid of losing people, and equally afraid of letting anyone close.
That is a hard contradiction to live with.
But his journey with Keerthana shows that vulnerability and growth can coexist.
You don't need every fear resolved before you start learning to love better.

## Vivek: The Most Understood
And then Vivek, the one I understood most deeply.

His insecurity, his ego, his fear of asking for help, his inability to admit a mistake, his constant need to prove himself: all painfully familiar.
The wish to make everything happen on your own, yet being too afraid to ask anyone.
The fear of what people will think, say, or assume.

But what hit hardest was the abandonment.
When something goes wrong, even something small, Vivek pulls away from everyone and everything.
Somewhere underneath is the quiet thought: maybe I am the problem.
So he leaves before he can be left, and calls it solitude instead of loneliness.

My ego has made me do many things like that.

He wants to fight, but can't face confrontation.
He wants people close, but pushes them away.
He wants to be understood, but keeps it all inside.
His perfectionism and ego become obstacles of their own.
And even when good things are right there, he struggles to believe he deserves them.

Vivek isn't just an insecure character.
He is every person fighting a battle nobody else can see.
Watching him, I realised I was one of them.

## The Beauty of Simplicity
My biggest takeaway from ENE Repeat is its love for everyday life.

The ordinary conversations.
The awkward pauses.
The stupid jokes.
The disagreements.
The little victories.
The insecurities we hide behind our egos.
The people who show up without being asked.

None of it feels important when it happens.
Yet it becomes the memory we carry for years.

Not every emotion needs a monologue.
Not every relationship needs a grand declaration.
Not every problem needs an extraordinary solution.
Sometimes all we need is a little understanding, a little patience, and someone willing to sit beside us.

The film doesn't only celebrate friendship.
It celebrates the imperfect people who make friendship worth having.

## Final Thoughts: Cinema, Life, and Everything in Between
I loved ENE Repeat, not just as a film but as an experience.

It reminded me why I love cinema: why stories matter, why characters stay with us, why music can make us feel what we can't explain, and why a filmmaker who watches ordinary human behaviour closely can create something extraordinary.

I walked in expecting a story about four friends.
I walked out thinking about friendship, love, insecurity, solitude, regret, perseverance, vulnerability, and the little things that make life worth living.

A film doesn't have to change your life.
Sometimes it only has to change the way you look at it.

If I could leave one thought, it would be this:

Somewhere inside each of us is someone holding on with both hands, long after his own hands have started to shake, because he cannot bear to watch what he loves come apart.

Someone who is knocked down again and again, and still gets up to celebrate the smallest light.

Someone who is terrified of losing the very people he keeps at arm's length.

And someone who would rather disappear quietly than say three small words: I need help.

They are not four strangers.
They are one heart, wearing four faces, learning slowly, painfully, and beautifully how to stay.

Perhaps life itself is one big film, with no retakes, no perfect script, and no guarantee of a happy ending.
We make mistakes, lose people, find people, hurt, heal, fall apart, and somehow keep going.

But if we are fortunate, we find a few people who make us want to keep the camera rolling.

And when the credits finally roll, what matters may not be how perfectly we played our roles, but how beautifully we made the journey worth remembering.

Somewhere, somehow, all of us are still figuring out life.
And that's okay.

ENE Repeat. A little bit of cinema, a little bit of life, and a whole lot of us.
poems.translation: The Insecurities, Imperfections, Fears, and More

poems.title: Kya Maine Pucha?
poems.text:
Kya maine pucha tha ki aao zindagi mein,
Kya maine kaha tha ki bas jao dil mein,
Tum khud hi bane the meri jeene ki wajah,
Ab kyun chhod gaye mujhe dard-e-tanhai mein?

Kya maine pucha tha ki kasmein hazaar do,
Meri berang duniya ko khushiyon se sanwaar do,
Maine toh bas tumhe apni duaon mein maanga tha,
Kya kaha tha ki mujhe umar bhar ka intezaar do?

Kya maine pucha tha ki khwaab dikha kar tod do,
Meri hansti hui aankhon ko ashkon se jod do,
Tumhare baad ab khud se bhi mohabbat nahi rahi,
Kya maine pucha tha ki mujhe mujhse hi juda kar do?

poems.title: She Shines
poems.text:
She shines like the moon, so bright and fair,
Her voice is like a melody, floating in the air,
Her fragrance is like flowers in full bloom,
Every smile of hers lights up the room.

Without her, my world feels tight and small,
With her presence, I feel I have it all.
Her laughter, so sweet, fills my heart with cheer,
In her smile, my happiness is always near.

She is a beauty like none before,
A symphony of grace, forevermore.
Her voice, a melody, soft and true,
Echoes in my heart, a love that grew.

Each sorrow she carries, a whisper of pain,
Yet in her embrace, I find peace again.
Her smile, a beacon and a guiding light,
Gives purpose to my days, and makes them bright.

Her energy flows, a wave so serene,
Her presence, a calm like I’ve never seen.
Her eyes, like stars, in the darkest night,
Sparkle with love, a radiant light.

Her gaze, a caress, tender and sweet,
A touch that makes my world complete.
Her love fills my heart with endless grace,
A unique tenderness, none can replace.

poems.title: Thousands See Her
poems.text:
Thousands see her, yet none perceive,
The way her presence makes me believe.
To them, she’s just a fleeting sight,
To me, she’s the sun, the stars, the night.

In crowds, she walks with effortless grace,
Yet I alone know what lies beneath that face.
The depth of kindness in her eyes so deep,
The gentle promises she makes and keeps.

She lights the world with her mere presence,
Yet remains humble, a quiet essence.
While others chase what glitters and gleams,
She fills the silence with whispered dreams.

A thousand hearts may see her beauty true,
But none will ever feel what I feel for you.

poems.title: Unseen, Yet Infinite
poems.note: A second telling of “Thousands See Her”
poems.text:
They speak to her with borrowed lines,
I carve my love in endless rhymes.
Many may chase, may long, may yearn,
But my heart for her will forever burn.

She’s not just beauty, she’s the air I breathe,
The sky I paint, the fate I weave.
They may admire, they may fall,
But my madness outshines them all.

poems.title: It Began with a Glance
poems.text:
It began with a glance so rare,
A spark of charm hung in the air.
In whispers soft, the rains did fall,
And love embraced us—heart and all.

A moment froze, a breath suspended,
Where two souls perfectly blended.
Your eyes held stories yet untold,
A warmth that put away the cold.

In that instant, time stood still,
Your presence bent my very will.
A glance transformed into a flame,
Nothing would ever be the same.

What started as a fleeting sight,
Became my guiding star, my light.

poems.title: In Her Eyes
poems.text:
In her eyes, I saw the sky so bright,
Her voice was soft, a sweet delight.
Her hair flowed gently, dark as night,
A smile so warm, it felt just right.

Every time her name came up, I’d blush and turn red,
Thinking of her, the warmth in me spread.
Every time she spoke, my heart would explode,
I wished it never ended, in that moment, I glowed.

She was sweet, caring, like a soft embrace,
Though the love I felt, she never could trace.
For unspoken feelings, deep and true,
Were the things I wished she only knew.

poems.title: Woh Ladki
poems.text:
Woh ladki… ek khwab thi, jo meri tanhaayi ka sach ban gayi,
Main uske husn ka qaid hoon, aur yeh qaid meri azaadi ban gayi,
Uski hansi mein chhupa hai mera saara khauf, mera saara sukoon,
Aur main… bas ek shayar, jo uske naam se apni umr likh raha hai.

poems.title: Junoon Ka Aisa Aalam
poems.translation: The seven stages of love — from a glance to annihilation
poems.text:
Dilkashi se hui shuruaat, ek nazar mein kho gaye,
Uns ki baarish mein bheege, har lamha Mohabbat ho gaye.
Mohabbat ne rukh badla, ab Aqeedat ki raah chali,
Ibadat ban gaya har ehsaas, har saans mein tera naam basi.

Junoon ka aisa aalam, khud se begaane ho gaye,
Maut bhi muskura uthi, jab tujhmein fana ho gaye.

poems.title: Pal Pal
poems.text:
Pal pal mere chain ko yun churaya aapne,
Ki na paas aaye, na hi door gaye.

Meri aankhon pe aisa jaadu chha gaya,
Ki aapko na chhod sakta hoon, na bhool sakta hoon.

Aise mere dil mein base ho aap,
Jaise Shyam mein basi ho Radha.

poems.title: Milo Ya Na Milo
poems.text:
मिलो या न मिलो तुम मेरे दिल में हमेशा बस जाओगे,
मेरी हर ख़ुशी और हर गम में तुम्ही रहोगे।
तुम्हारी यादों में मैं रात भर जागता हूँ,
और तुम्हारी ख़ुशी की ख़ातिर सब कुछ भूल जाता हूँ।

तुम्हारी मुस्कुराहट ही मेरी ज़िंदगी है,
तुम्हारी गर्मा गर्मी में ही मेरी क़िस्मत है।
मिलो या न मिलो, पर मेरे साथ हमेशा रहना,
क्योंकि तुम मेरी साँसों में, मेरी हर धड़कन में हो।

poems.title: I Miss You
poems.text:
I miss you when the sun shines bright,
And even more in silent night.
I miss the thought of seeing you the next day,
The little things I used to do to make you stay.

I miss the way I would search around,
Hoping you were to be found.
The silly reasons I would make,
Just to talk, for my heart’s sake.

I walked behind, yet stayed unseen,
Imagining things that might have been.
The way you smiled, the way you stared,
Moments I wished that you had cared.

But now the days feel cold and long,
Without you here, it all feels wrong.
I miss it all, the thrill, the cheer,
And most of all, I miss you near.

poems.title: The Night Goes On
poems.text:
I count the stars, one by one,
The night is long, but sleep won’t come.
I close my eyes, but all I see,
Are memories of you and me.

I miss your voice, I miss your smile,
I wish you’d stay, just for a while.
My heart feels lost, my world is blue,
I don’t know how to live without you.

The night goes on, but time stands still,
I miss you more, I always will.
I hope one day, you will miss me too,
And find your way back, like I want you to.

poems.title: Echoes of You
poems.text:
The stars above still spell your name,
Though time has blurred the burning flame.
I trace the sky and wish you knew,
That every echo leads to you.

poems.title: Fading Footsteps
poems.text:
The paths we walked now stand so still,
The echoes lost against my will.
Each step we took, so full of light,
Now fades into the endless night.

poems.title: Mere Intezaar Ka Diya
poems.text:
न चाँद का छाँव मिला, न सूरज की धूप मिली,
मैं तो बस साँझ की हल्की रोशनी में तेरा इंतेज़ार किए बैठा हूँ।
मैंने तेरा इंतेज़ार किया है, कर रहा हूँ और करता रहूँगा,
चाहे तू आए या न आए, मेरे इंतेज़ार का दिया यूँही जलता रहेगा।

तेरे आने की बाट जोहता हूँ हर पल,
तेरी यादों में बिताता हूँ हर लम्हा, हर पल।
हज़ार बार हार मान लेता हूँ, पर फिर से उठ जाता हूँ,
क्योंकि तुम ही मेरी ज़िंदगी हो, तुम ही मेरी मुराद हो।

poems.title: Jo Socha Tha
poems.text:
जो सोचा था, वो बन न सका,
जो चाहा था, वो पास न रहा।
हर राह में बस अँधेरा मिला,
धड़कन में एक तन्हा सवेरा मिला।

तुम्हारी राह में सब कुछ खोया,
पर तुम्हारी यादों में सब कुछ पाया।
तुम्हारे बिना ज़िंदगी सूनी है,
पर तुम्हारे साथ ज़िंदगी पूरी है।

इस साहिल पर अकेले खड़े हैं,
तुम्हारी आहट का इंतेज़ार है।
जब तक तुम न आओ, यह दिल न रुकेगा,
तुम्हारे आने का ख़्वाब न टूटेगा।

poems.title: Woh Chaandni Thi
poems.text:
वह चाँदनी थी, जो मेरी ज़िंदगी में रोशनी लाई,
और मैं एक था जो उनके ख्वाब लेकर रह गया।
उसने दोस्ती के अरमान लेकर दिल में बस गई,
और मैंने उसका मोहब्बत का जहान खुद में बसाया।

हर पल उसके साथ एक ख्वाब था,
हर बात उसकी ज़िंदगी का खिताब था।
पर क़िस्मत ने कुछ और ही सोचा था,
और वह दूर चली गई, पर दिल में रह गई।

poems.title: Zamana Chhod Diya
poems.translation: The world let go of me
poems.text:
ज़माना छोड़ दिया मेरा साथ,
शाम-ए-ग़म ने दिया मुझे हाथ।
क़िस्मत यूँ बदल गई मेरी,
जब देखी मैंने चेहरा तेरी।

तेरी मुस्कुराहट ने सदा सुनाई,
तेरे प्यार में हर रात लगाई।
तेरी याद में रातें हों बिताई,
तेरी ख़ुशी ही मेरी ख़ुशी आई।

poems.title: Purani Aadat
poems.text:
Teri khamoshi mein ab meri awaaz kyun nahi rehti…
Kya main ab bhi teri zindagi ka hissa hoon,
Ya sirf ek purani aadat?

poems.title: She Stood Like the Sun
poems.text:
She stood like the sun, steady and bright,
While I, a dreamer, lost in my night.
Her words were simple, her heart was kind,
But I wove stories within my mind.

She offered friendship, a bond so pure,
Yet I dreamed of a life, of something more.
Her laughter, her presence, a gentle breeze,
But I chased horizons she…

poems.title: A Love Unsaid
poems.text:
The words I never dared to tell,
Still linger where my heart once fell.
If time could give a second chance,
I…

poems.title: If I See You Again
poems.text:
If I see you again,
will I be the storm that learned your name,
or the silence that forgot your face?

Will I hate you
for the nights that stitched loneliness into my skin,
or love you harder
because some wounds bloom instead of fade?

Will I fight you
with every shattered promise we left behind,
or fight for you
like a fool chasing a sunrise that never waits?

Perhaps I’ll walk away,
leaving your shadow to haunt empty streets,
while my heart lingers behind,
still calling yours in a language broken by goodbye.

I want you.
That is my sweetest tragedy.

I fear you.
That is my cruelest truth.

Because loving you
felt like holding a flame in winter.
It kept me alive
while quietly turning me to ash.

So if fate is reckless enough
to let our eyes meet again,

don’t ask what I’ll choose.

My heart has buried you a thousand times,
yet every lonely night
it still kneels beside your memory,
placing fresh flowers
on a love that never learned how to die.

poems.title: Mohabbat Ka Ilzaam
poems.text:
Mohabbat ka ilzaam sab seh liya,
Dil bechara khud hi lut gaya.
Jis haath ne ujaale diye the mujhe,
Ussi haath ne aag bhi laga diya.

Ek pal mein sajaya tha jo dil ka shehar,
Wohi pal mein usne mita bhi diya.
Wafa ki raahon mein chhod kar mujhe,
Woh khud hi khuda ban gaya.

poems.title: Dawa Se Bhi Darta Hoon
poems.translation: Now I fear even the cure
poems.text:
Dard aisa zehar diya mujhe,
Ke ab dawa se bhi darta hoon.
Shab-e-gham mein tanha bhatakta hoon,
Ke ab har nayi subah se darta hoon.

Bhool jaane ka waqt aaya,
To sajdon mein usi ko yaad karta hoon.
Jise kab ka kho chuka hoon,
Aaj bhi usi pe marta hoon.

poems.title: Yehi Meri Wafa Hai
poems.text:
Pyaar mein Khuda jo dekh liya maine,
Har sajde mein tera noor dekh liya maine.

Jaane waalon ko na roka,
Lekin unki khushiyon ki hifazat ki maine.
Apni hasraton ko dafan karke,
Unki muskurahat ki ibaadat ki maine.

Ishq agar yehi hai…
To yehi meri dua hai…
Dard agar yehi hai…
To yehi meri wafa hai…

Har din aur har raat,
Yunhi jee liya maine.
Har saans mein uska naam,
Khamoshi se le liya maine.

Ye kaisi mohabbat likhi tune…
Jeete ji qabr dikha di tune…

Na usse shikayat hai,
Na tujhe ilzaam deta hoon.
Bas itna samajh na paaya,
Mohabbat ka anjaam kyun deta hoon.

Log kehte hain,
Waqt sab kuch bhula deta hai.
Mujhe to har guzarta lamha,
Uski yaad aur gehri kar deta hai.

poems.title: Khamoshi Hi Meri Zubaan
poems.text:
Main ab unhe awaaz nahin deta hoon…
Kyun? Kyunki agar woh mud kar aa gaye,
To main unki khushi ka qaatil ban jaunga.
Aur agar na aaye…
To qayamat tak aise hi bikhar jaunga.

Isliye…
Ab yeh khamoshi hi meri zubaan hai…
Intezaar hi meri zindagi…
Aur dard hi meri pehchaan…

poems.title: Aansuon Se Likha
poems.text:
Main usko aansuon se likh raha hoon,
Taaki mere baad koi aur na padh paaye.

poems.title: Main Hoon Kaun
poems.text:
Aakhir main hoon kaun, sab karne ki zid pe ada hua bachcha,
Ya waqt ke haathon haar gaya, khud se hi lada hua bachcha.
Khwahishein toh hazaar hain, par haathon mein kuch bhi nahi,
Main woh insaan hoon jo jeena chahta hai… par jee nahi raha kabhi.

poems.title: The Monster
poems.text:
I was never the monster they painted in flame,
Just a whisper of truth with a villain’s name.
In shadows I walked where their judgments grew,
But the darkness they feared was the light I knew.

poems.title: The Morning
poems.text:
Each morning I wake with a weight on my chest,
A life still breathing, a heart laid to rest.
The sun drags the day through a colorless sky,
While something inside me quietly dies.

The hours crawl past like a slow bleeding wound,
A life half-lived in a hollow cocoon.
No scream, no fire, no thunder to prove,
Just time carving pieces of me as it moves.

And night always comes like a cold, final thief,
Counting the ruins of another day’s grief.
Then sleep takes the rest of whatever was left,
So morning can wake me… a little more dead.

poems.title: Alone I Stand
poems.text:
Alone I stand, with heart in hand,
Hoping someone will understand.
A quiet soul, a silent plea,
To see the real side of me.

In crowds of many, I feel so lost,
The price of solitude, that I paid the cost.
Looking for a soul who cares so deep,
Someone to hold me, to make me weep.

With joy, not sorrow, but from the core,
Someone who will love me forevermore.
A companion, a friend, a soulmate true,
Someone to turn my grey skies blue.

Until that day, I’ll wait and see,
If someone’s out there meant for me.

poems.title: Main Duniya Ko Samajh Chuka Hoon
poems.text:
Main duniya ko samajh chuka hoon,
Har raaz, har kahani jaan chuka hoon.
Phir bhi dhokha khaakar haar gaya hoon.

poems.title: The Pursuit
poems.text:
We chase the horizon, forever seeking the new,

poems.title: Rise and Reach
poems.text:
Rain or sky, don’t let a day slip by,
Keep moving forward, reach for what’s high.
Through every challenge, through every fight,
Push ahead—chase and embrace the light.

When clouds hang low and the world feels slow,
Rise above, let your spirit glow.
No day is wasted, no time stands still,
Keep climbing higher and trust your will.

When shadows linger and winds grow strong,
Stand your ground for you’ve been brave all along.
No time is lost, no dream will fade,
Rise with courage and be unafraid.

So keep on going, reach for the height,
For rain or sky, never let a day slip by.

poems.title: I Was in Darkness
poems.text:
I was in darkness, wanted to be alone,
But by your light, a warmth was shown.

poems.title: తను ఆకాశ వీధిలో అందాల జాబిలి
poems.translation: Anaganaga oka Mahanati — a tribute to Actress Savitri
poems.text:
ఒక పాత్రతో వర్ణించలేము...
ఒక మాటతో చెప్పలేము...
ఆమె గురించి రాయాలంటే
జ్ఞాపకాలే కలం పట్టాలి.

నవ్వితే వెన్నెల కూడా
తన వెలుగును మరిచిపోయేది.
ఏడిస్తే తెర ముందు కూర్చున్న
ప్రతి హృదయం తడిసిపోయేది.

ఆమె కళ్లలో మాటలుండేవి,
ఆమె మౌనంలో కథలుండేవి.
ఆమె తెరపై కనిపిస్తే
ఒక పాత్ర కాదు...
ఒక జీవితం కనిపించేది.

ఆమె అందాన్ని వర్ణించడానికి
కవులకు పదాలు చాలలేదు.
ఆమెను గానంలో బంధించడానికి
గాయకులకు పాటలు చాలలేదు.
ఆమె నటనను కొలవడానికి
కాలానికి సంవత్సరాలు చాలలేదు.

ఎన్నో పేర్లు
కాలనదిలో అలలా వచ్చి వెళ్లిపోయాయి...
కానీ కొన్ని పేర్లు మాత్రమే
కాలం అనే పుస్తకంలో
చెరిగిపోని అక్షరాలవుతాయి.

ఎప్పుడు ఎక్కడ పాత సినిమా చూసినా
ఒక జ్ఞాపకమై వస్తుంది.
పాత పాట వినిపించినా
ఒక రూపమై కళ్లముందు నిలుస్తుంది.

ఆమెను తలుచుకుంటే అనిపిస్తుంది...
కొంతమంది మనుషులు
భూమిపై కొన్నేళ్లు మాత్రమే ఉంటారు,
కానీ మనసుల్లో మాత్రం
శాశ్వతంగా ఉండిపోతారు అని.

బిరుదులు ఎన్ని వచ్చినా,
గౌరవాలు ఎన్ని దక్కినా,
కథను పైవాడు ఎలా రాసినా,
జీవితాన్ని కాలం ఎలా మలిచినా,
తను మాత్రం
మర్చిపోలేని ఒక అందమైన స్మృతి.

దేవదాసులో పార్వతిగా,
మిస్సమ్మలో మేరీగా,
మాయాబజార్‌లో సుందరిగా,
ప్రతి హృదయంలో చిరస్థాయిగా.

తను ఆకాశ వీధిలో అందాల జాబిలి...
అనగనగా ఒక మహానటి.

fragments.line: some wounds bloom instead of fade
The stars above still spell your name
a love that never learned how to die
To me, she’s the sun, the stars, the night.
the darkness they feared was the light I knew
Main usko aansuon se likh raha hoon
I miss you more, I always will.
like holding a flame in winter
Maut bhi muskura uthi, jab tujhmein fana ho gaye
Rise with courage and be unafraid.
So morning can wake me… a little more dead.
Now fades into the endless night.

prologue.label: Prologue
prologue.text: I write what I cannot say out loud. These are small confessions — of a *glance* that became a *flame*, of a *lamp* of *waiting* that never went out, of mornings that woke me a little more *dead*, and of a *love* that never learned how to *die*.

it still kneels beside your memory,

about.lede: A notebook, a sleepless night, and every language I know — all trying to say one thing.
story: I started writing the way most people do — to survive a feeling that had nowhere else to go. A glance that became a flame. A friendship I wished were something more. A morning heavier than the night before it.
Some poems arrived in *English*. Some only knew how to be said in *Hindi and Urdu*. And one came in *Telugu*, for Savitri — the Mahanati, whose films outlived their decades.

This was an old hobby, and I hadn’t opened these notebooks in months. But a poem left unread is a lamp left unlit. So here they are — every one of them, even the ones that stop mid-sentence — *set in motion*.
interlude: Some of these poems end mid‑sentence.
